quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 total revenue was $137.2 million, up 43% from $95.5 million a year ago; infrastructure (approximately $63 million) is now the largest revenue category, growing 136% year-over-year on production ramps in optical data center platforms. Broadband was approximately $44 million, connectivity approximately $19 million, industrial multi-market approximately $12 million; non-GAAP gross margin 59.5%.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $137.2 million, up 43% YoY; infrastructure approximately $63 million, up 136% YoY; non-GAAP gross margin 59.5%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'Based on customer orders and rising visibility of the program ramps, we are increasing our expectations for 2026 optical data center revenue to $150 million-$170 million range', and expects a step function data center revenue increase beginning in Q2 with upside as run rates expand into 2027. He attributed the raise to timing of ramps across both 400G and 800G at a number of customers after an initially conservative guide.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 optical data center revenue $150 million-$170 million

quarterly_data.signal: Keystone PAM4 DSP optical transceiver platform is ramping at multiple major hyperscale customers across both the U.S. and Asia, supporting 400G and 800G PAM4 deployments for scale-up and scale-out. Design wins span all the module vendors; hyperscaler exposure comes both from hyperscaler-owned designs qualified directly and through module vendors ('Both'). CEO: 'we are only halfway there to our end data center diversification across all the hyperscalers'; ramps will concentrate on a few customers, with other data centers coming online into 2027. Both U.S. and China hyperscalers are deploying PAM4 DSPs very rapidly.

At OFC, MaxLinear showcased its 1.6 Tb data center platform: Rushmore (200 Gb per lane PAM4 DSP), Washington (matching 200 Gb per lane TIA) and Annapurna (1.6 Tb AEC and 3.2 Tb onboard electrical retimer platform for scale-up), positioned for LPO, LRO, AECs, XPO and co-packaged optics. Customer engagement on Rushmore 'has accelerated faster than expected'; production ramps anticipated beginning in late 2026 with strong growth through 2027. Rushmore and Washington are sampling. MaxLinear acknowledges it is not first to 1.6 Tb versus two incumbent competitors, but expects higher 1.6 Tb ASPs to lift revenue and gross margin as mix shifts. Annapurna retimer is currently Ethernet-based.
quarterly_data.figure: Rushmore production ramps beginning in late 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CEO sizing of scale-up vs scale-out: 'the optical transceivers, 30% of the market is for scale up' and '70% is for scale out today.' MaxLinear's scale-up participation comes from optical transceivers plus the new 1.6 Tb onboard electrical retimers and AECs. TAM ranking: optical transceiver DSPs first by far, electrical retimers second, AECs third. On CPO/LPO/LRO: 'I think we are three years or so away from determining that'; today it is a very small share of silicon units and not expected to be a huge part of revenue. If CPO is bare bones, the TIA and driver is a natural fit.
quarterly_data.figure: optical transceivers 30% scale up / 70% scale out

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 guidance: revenue between $160 million and $170 million, with growth from all four segments and particular strength in infrastructure driven by data center optical interconnects; non-GAAP gross margin in the range of 58% and 61%. CFO kept the guide cautious on input costs: 'wafer cost, packaging, et cetera, are moving up', costs the industry has been able to pass along; 800G and 1.6 Tb carry higher gross margins.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $160 million and $170 million; non-GAAP gross margin 58% and 61%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 exit cash of approximately $89.9 million; the primary use of cash was a substantial prepayment for wafers supporting rising demand for data center low geometry products, for which order backlog is increasing in the second half. CFO on supply: 'there's some supply constraints out there. I think we planned well for this and worked really closely with the partners'; further prepayments possible as demand improves; backlog starting to build into 2027. The expiring revolver was renewed and taken up slightly.
quarterly_data.figure: cash approximately $89.9 million after wafer prepayment

quarterly_data.signal: Expanding hyperscale data center footprint beyond PAM4: first XGS-PON design win at a U.S. hyperscale data center through a Tier 1 OEM partner (dedicated PON-based control plane across data centers); ramp expected sometime in 2027, TAM expected to expand to 'over hundreds of millions of dollars'. Also won USB bridge controller designs with two major hyperscalers for rack-level AI system management. Panther 5 storage accelerator is sampling with key customers.
